data.body:
SAFETY NET LANDED AND APPLIED. Gerrit 1326 is MERGED, and the Bedrock client-error alarm now EXISTS IN CLOUDWATCH, not just in HCL — which is the distinction bug 1c39 exists to make.

MERGE, with the SHA re-derived rather than assumed. Gerrit rewrites SHAs on submit, so I looked the commit up by its trailer: 'git log gerrit/main --grep=rebar-ticket: eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a' -> 1f48330f2d 'eb6e: Bedrock safety net and packaging' (the pushed revision was 01aab994fe; they differ, as expected). Submit needed an explicit JSON body: POST /a/changes/1326/submit with no body returns HTTP 400 'Expected JSON object'; with -d '{}' it returns 200 and status MERGED. Worth recording because the 400 looks like a permission problem and is not.

MIRROR LAG OBSERVED, exactly as the inherited handoff warns. Immediately after the merge, origin/main (the GitHub mirror) was still 1920dc9fe5 and did NOT contain infra/terraform/monitoring_eb6e.tf, while gerrit/main was 1f48330f2d and did. I applied from a worktree at the GERRIT commit rather than waiting on the mirror. Operational consequence to remember for the flip: autodeploy fetches from the MIRROR (MIRROR_URL=https://github.com/navapbc/rebar.git), so the container rebuild lags replication, not the Gerrit submit.

Also noted: main had independently advanced two commits (15e505200d, 1920dc9fe5) from another workstream while my stack was in review, so Gerrit rebased server-side. That is additional drift against the epic's own attestation, which will need a fresh review before 061c closes.

THE APPLY was surgical. From a clean worktree at 1f48330f2d: 'Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy', the single resource being aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.bedrock_invoke_client_errors. Applied, exit 0, and the RE-PLAN afterwards returns exit 0 'No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration.' So the drift this landing would otherwise have created (per 1c39) is closed in the same sitting.

ALARM ARN (criterion: recorded):
    arn:aws:cloudwatch:us-east-1:896586841071:alarm:rebar-bedrock-invoke-client-errors
Configuration as applied, read back from CloudWatch rather than from the HCL: threshold 0.25, GreaterThanThreshold, evaluation_periods 2, treat_missing_data notBreaching, and BOTH AlarmActions AND OKActions = [arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:896586841071:rebar-gerrit-alerts]. The actions are there because I caught them MISSING in review — the file had been modelled on monitoring_s4b.tf, which turns out to carry the real defect now tracked as 9baf.

NOT SITTING IN INSUFFICIENT_DATA — and satisfied by REAL DATA, not by my forcing it. The alarm history's own record:
    16:33:22 -0700  StateUpdate  'Alarm updated from INSUFFICIENT_DATA to OK'
That transition happened ON ITS OWN, roughly one minute after creation and BEFORE any set-alarm-state call of mine, which means CloudWatch found datapoints for the metric-math expression. This is the criterion's actual intent: an alarm on a metric nothing publishes would have stayed INSUFFICIENT_DATA. Corroborated independently by the authoring agent's read-only get-metric-data validation of the same expression over a 6-hour window — StatusCode Complete, a datapoint in ALL 24 of the 900s periods, and the denominator genuinely 0.0 in 15 of them, which also proves the FILL + IF(e2>0,...) divide-by-zero guard on live data rather than by inspection.
CALIBRATION NOTE, carried from the 34cd alarm earlier today: my FIRST read of this alarm, seconds after apply, was 'INSUFFICIENT_DATA / Unchecked: Initial alarm creation'. Reading it then and concluding the metric does not exist would have been wrong. A freshly created alarm reads INSUFFICIENT_DATA for reasons that have nothing to do with whether its metric publishes.

FORCED TEST NOTIFICATION (criterion: recorded), and confirmed DELIVERED rather than merely configured. The SNS topic has exactly one CONFIRMED subscription (protocol email, endpoint joeoakhart@navapbc.com, a real subscription ARN rather than PendingConfirmation), so a notification has somewhere to go. Then, from the alarm's own history:
    16:33:35.862  StateUpdate  'Alarm updated from OK to ALARM'      (forced by me, reason text marks it a DRILL)
    16:33:35.900  Action       'Successfully executed action arn:aws:sns:...:rebar-gerrit-alerts'
    16:34:04.822  StateUpdate  'Alarm updated from ALARM to OK'      (returned; also exercises ok_actions)
    16:34:04.861  Action       'Successfully executed action arn:aws:sns:...:rebar-gerrit-alerts'
    16:33:22.323  Action       'Successfully executed action arn:aws:sns:...:rebar-gerrit-alerts'   (the real INSUFFICIENT_DATA->OK transition)
Three separate 'Successfully executed action' records. I am citing CloudWatch's own execution record rather than the AWS/SNS NumberOfNotificationsDelivered metric, which still read 0 at the time of the check — SNS metrics lag by minutes, and reading that 0 as 'not delivered' would have been the same mistake as reading the initial INSUFFICIENT_DATA as 'no metric'. The alarm is currently OK.

STILL OUTSTANDING on the ordering criterion: item (c), the induced VOTER_ERROR transition of rebar-gerrit-voter-errors on the pre-cutover Anthropic path. The bot is still on Anthropic (1327, the flip, is NOT submitted). The drill is pre-registered above and now scripted with idempotent induce/restore, an explicit both-directions reachability proof from inside the container, and a probe-force so it does not wait out the 5-minute timer.
